title: Help Me, O Lord! Behold, I Enter
description: Help Me, O Lord! Behold, I Enter in Tonic Solfa to NEUMARK, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Johann Rist wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 171.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 9.8.9.8.8.8, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to NEUMARK; any other 9.8.9.8.8.8 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Help me, O Lord! Be-hold, I en-ter Up-on an-oth-er year to day; In Thee my hopes and thoughts now cen-ter, Re-new my cou-rage for the way: New life, new strength, new happ-i-ness I ask of Thee, O hear and bless!

lines: Help me, O Lord! Behold, I enter
Upon another year to-day;
In Thee my hopes and thoughts now center,
Renew my courage for the way:
New life, new strength, new happiness
I ask of Thee, O hear and bless!
May every plan and undertaking
This year be all begun with Thee;
When I am sleeping or am waking,
Still let me know Thou art with me;
Abroad do Thou my footsteps guide,
At home be ever at my side.
Be this a time of grace and pardon;
Thy rod I take with willing mind,
But suffer naught my heart to harden;
O let me now Thy mercy find;
In Thee alone, my God, I live,
Thou only canst my sins forgive.
And may this year to me be holy;
Thy grace so fill my every thought
That all my life be pure and lowly
And truthful as a Christian’s ought;
So make me, while yet dwelling here,
Pious and blest from year to year.
And grant, Lord, when the year is over,
That it for me in peace may close;
In all things care for me and cover
My head in time of fear and woes;
So may I, when my years are gone,
Appear with joy before Thy throne.

licence: Public domain: Johann Rist died in 1667; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Johann Rist (1607–1667), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to NEUMARK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
